episode_title: An AI state of the union: We've passed the inflection point, dark factories are coming, and automation timelines
summary: 1 hour 40 min. Simon Willison on why November 2025 was the inflection point for coding agents; his three agentic engineering patterns (red/green TDD, templates, hoarding); the 'dark factory' pattern where AI does its own QA without human review; writes 95% of code from his phone. YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wc8FBhQtdsA

episode_title: How Intercom 2x'd their engineering velocity in 9 months with Claude Code
summary: 1 hr 19 min. Hosted by Claire Vo. Intercom doubled merged PRs per R&D employee in 9 months. 100% of engineers plus non-engineers shipping code via Claude Code. 13 plugins, 100+ skills. Telemetry infrastructure for measuring AI adoption. Production-safe hooks (read-replica DB access, Okta auth, DynamoDB audit trail).

episode_title: Paper's vision for the future of design tooling
summary: Stephen Haney discusses how Paper fundamentally changes the speed of traditional design flows by putting code components onto a design canvas with real React and Tailwind, enabling designers to export production-ready components.

episode_title: The 2026 AI Design Field Report (tools, process, and what's working)
summary: Field report on how top design teams are using AI in 2026. Covers tools, process changes, and what's actually working vs hype.

episode_title: Steve Yegge's Vibe Coding Manifesto — Why Claude Code Is the Future
summary: Steve Yegge discusses why the 2024 tech stack is becoming obsolete, the importance of trusting agents, and orchestrating agents like a 'NASCAR pit crew' as a shift away from traditional IDE-based development.

episode_title: Brian Scanlan: Building AI-First at Intercom
summary: Deeper technical discussion of Intercom's AI-first engineering transformation, focusing on the Ruby on Rails backend context and how Claude Code integrates with production systems.
Boris Cherny (creator of Claude Code) and Cat Wu (PM) on Claude Code's origins as an internal hack, its architecture, and roadmap. First deep technical interview about Claude Code.

episode_title: Head of Claude Code: What happens after coding is solved
summary: Boris Cherny on the post-coding future, Claude Code's growth to 4% of public GitHub commits, and what comes next when AI handles routine coding.

episode_title: The Creators of Model Context Protocol
summary: David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers on MCP's origins, design decisions, and protocol evolution. The canonical technical deep-dive on MCP.

episode_title: Extreme Harness Engineering: 1M LOC, 1B toks/day, 0% human code, 0% human review
summary: Ryan Lopopolo on building a 1M LOC codebase with zero human-written or reviewed code. Defines 'Harness Engineering' as the structured constraints that make this possible. Highly relevant to repo-template-governance.

summary: John Lindquist (Claude Code Ambassador at Vercel) demos advanced techniques: context loading via mermaid diagrams, stop hooks, automated code quality checks. Practical skills-focused episode.

episode_title: The internal AI tool that's transforming how Stripe designs products
summary: Owen Williams (design manager, Stripe) on Protodash — Stripe's internal AI prototyping platform. Shows how a design team built a full prototyping studio on top of Cursor rules + React components.
Amelia Wattenberger on Intent (her Augment Code product) and what developer workspaces look like when agents do most of the work. Directly addresses the unified-project-layer pain point.
